svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Propose, then commit: the three barriers on every calendar write
svg.desc: A write starts with the assistant calling the tool with no approval token. Barrier one is the allowlist, checked in memory before any network call. The connector then reads the records back from Odoo and returns a proposal with a signed token that expires in fifteen minutes. A coordinator approves. Barrier two verifies the signature, the expiry, and that the operation, model, ids and values match the token. Barrier three asks for confirmation again at the moment of execution. Only then does the write reach Odoo. Any barrier failing means nothing is written.
svg.text: PHASE 1 · PROPOSE
Claude calls the tool
Planning stages are read-only, so a write always starts a separate, approved step.
BARRIER 1 · GOVERNANCE
The allowlist, checked in memory. Model, field or file absent means denied.
Checked before anything leaves the process, so it holds on every run.
The connector reads the records back from Odoo
Current title, start, stop and attendees, so the proposal shows real values.
A proposal, plus a signed token that expires in 15 minutes
Each field as it stands against what it would become, the ids, and who gets emailed.
Nothing has been written.
PHASE 2 · COMMIT
A person approves
The coordinator reviews the proposal and approves. Every write passes through here.
BARRIER 2 · TOKEN
Signature, expiry, operation, model, ids and a hash of the values.
An approval covers exactly the operation and records it was given for.
BARRIER 3 · CONFIRMATION
Asked again at the moment of execution, so the person stays in control to the last step.
The write reaches Odoo once a person has approved it, and only then.
